title: Beyond Field-Line Descriptions: Unintended Antennas, EMC, and Signal Integrity
content: Unintended electromagnetic radiation and coupling arise when conductors, cables, traces, enclosures, and other structures support current and voltage distributions that allow them to behave partially as antennas. Conventional electromagnetic compatibility and signal-integrity theory describes these effects through impedance, common-mode and differential-mode currents, parasitic capacitance and inductance, transmission-line behavior, resonance, shielding, grounding, near-field coupling, and radiated emissions. These methods provide the quantitative foundation for engineering analysis. This article develops a complementary structural interpretation within the Beyond Field-Line Descriptions framework. The proposed Photony model treats unintended radiating structures as distributed electron-transduction systems in which internal electrons predominantly support magnetic structuring associated with current, while surface-associated electrons predominantly support electric structuring associated with voltage and surface charge. Geometry, discontinuities, conductor length, return-path configuration, and frequency determine where these structures become concentrated, reflected, redistributed, or released. Particular attention is given to unintended antenna formation, common-mode excitation, conductor and cable asymmetry, standing-wave development, surface localization, and the transition from source-coupled electromagnetic structuring to unwanted outward radiation or coupling. Signal-integrity effects are interpreted as changes in the spatial and temporal organization of the same electromagnetic energy that conventional theory describes through fields, voltages, currents, and Poynting transport. The framework is intended as a structural interpretation of established EMC and signal-integrity behavior rather than a replacement for conventional equations.
